name: Triangle-and-Two
idea: Two defenders stick to the two best shooters, and the other three guard a triangle by the basket.
why: Some teams have two great shooters. In a triangle-and-two, those shooters always have a defender right on them, and the triangle protects the paint, so the players who aren't great shooters are left to shoot from outside.
tryit: Chasers: stay close enough to touch your shooter, everywhere they go. Triangle: move together toward the ball, and shout “Shot!” to box out.

frames.say: You’re on defense, in a *triangle-and-two*. {X1} and {X2} stick to the two best shooters. {X3}, {X4} and {X5} make a triangle by the basket.
{3} passes to {4} in the corner. The triangle slides toward the ball, and {X4} steps out toward {4}.
The shooters run around to get open, but {X1} and {X2} stay right with them.
Nobody can pass to a shooter, so {4} has to shoot from the corner, with {X4} right there. Miss!
{X5} grabs the rebound! The shooters never got the ball, and the triangle protected the paint.
